source_document.body:
Ineos Grenadier Fieldmaster Edition (Photo: Calreyn88/Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, cropped)
The French factory Mercedes built for the tiny Smart city car, and that Jim Ratcliffe turned into the home of his Land Rover Defender tribute, could soon be building BYDs.
BYD confirmed today that it has entered exclusive negotiations to acquire Ineos Automotive’s plant in Hambach, France. If it closes, it would be the Chinese giant’s second passenger car factory in the EU after Hungary, and the first time a Chinese automaker buys an existing car plant in Europe.
Ineos is following its customers to the US
The other half of the deal is Ineos packing up. Alongside the announcement, Ineos Automotive said it plans to move Grenadier and Quartermaster production to the US, which it says accounts for about 70% of its sales. It has shortlisted US sites, hasn’t named any, and is aiming to start production there in 2028.
The math is simple. Every Grenadier shipped from France to the US gets hit with a 15% tariff, and the Quartermaster pickup falls under the 25% tariff on imported pickups. When 7 out of 10 of your customers are American, building your trucks in Lorraine stops making sense.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Ineos says it will keep building both models at Hambach “for the medium term” if the sale goes through, so the two companies would share the site for a while.
Neither side disclosed a price or a closing date, and the sale still has to go through consultation with employee representatives. BYD will soon find out that France is nothing like China when it comes to employee representation. There’s also no word yet on which BYD models would come out of Hambach or when. Same for the plant’s roughly 1,000 employees: BYD made no commitment on how many it would keep.
BYD executive vice president Stella Li said the company wants to give European consumers “vehicles built in France” that use BYD’s technology.
A small plant with a long history
Hambach opened in 1997 as “Smartville,” Mercedes’ factory for the Smart Fortwo, and it later built the all-electric Smart EQ Fortwo. Ineos bought it from Mercedes at the end of 2020 after dropping its plan to build a new factory in Wales, and Grenadier production started in 2022. Ineos says it has put nearly €540 million into the site since 2019.
Capacity is about 30,000 Grenadiers a year. That’s not much by BYD’s standards. BYD sold 3,561,615 passenger vehicles globally in the first 10 months of the year, which means 30,000 units is less than three days of its output.
There’s also a bit of irony in who’s buying. Ineos unveiled its first EV, the Fusilier, in early 2024 while romanticizing gas cars at the same event . A few months later, it shelved the electric model indefinitely, blaming “reluctant consumer uptake” of EVs. Now it’s selling its only factory to the world’s largest EV maker.
BYD’s European factory shopping spree
This isn’t a surprise. Back in May, Stella Li said BYD was in talks with Stellantis and “other companies too” to take over underused plants in Europe, and that BYD would rather own and run a plant than form a joint venture. Hambach fits that description exactly.
BYD’s first European car plant, in Szeged, Hungary , started trial production earlier this year and is expected to reach mass production in early 2027, with the Dolphin Surf and Atto 2 first in line. BYD eventually wants more than 150,000 vehicles a year out of it. Its separate factory project in Turkey has been put on pause.
The motivation is regulatory. China-built BYD EVs face a 17% countervailing duty in the EU on top of the standard 10% car tariff, imported Chinese hybrids are now subject to quotas, and the EU’s proposed “Made in Europe” rules would tie EV subsidies and public contracts to how much of a vehicle is built locally. A French plant solves a lot of those problems at once.
And BYD isn’t alone. Leapmotor started building the B10 at Stellantis’ Zaragoza plant in Spain in October, Dongfeng plans to build cars at a Stellantis factory in France, Geely is reportedly lining up a Ford plant in Spain, and Chery already assembles vehicles in Barcelona.
Chery is the one BYD should watch. Through October, BYD registered 320,445 vehicles in Europe, up 133%, according to Automotive News. Chery Group was just ahead with 320,631, up 235%. A gap of 186 cars.
Europe matters more than ever for BYD because home isn’t going well. BYD brand sales in China fell 40% to 1,544,699 vehicles over the first 10 months, and its global passenger vehicle sales are down 2.7%.
Electrek’s Take
This is a smart, cheap move for BYD. Building Szeged took years, including land disputes with private owners. Hambach comes with a trained workforce, a paint shop, a supplier base on the German border, and a seller that’s motivated to leave. You don’t get a much easier entry into France, but the easiest in France is still probably more difficult than anything BYD faced in China when it comes to deploying new production capacity.
The 30,000-unit capacity is small, but BYD isn’t buying it for what it builds today. It’s buying a “Made in France” label ahead of local content rules.

We also can’t ignore the symmetry here. Ineos is leaving Europe to build in the US because of tariffs. BYD is buying into Europe because of tariffs. That’s protectionism moving factories. Europe keeps the jobs, and the workers who used to build Smart EVs might get to build EVs again.
And yes, it’s funny that BYD is moving into the home of the Grenadier, a vehicle that exists because Ratcliffe loved the old Defender, days after a court in The Hague barred BYD’s Ti7 from the EU for infringing Land Rover’s Defender design.
The real question is what BYD puts on the line in Hambach. If it’s battery-electric cars, great. If it’s plug-in hybrids built to get around quotas, Europe is trading one gas-burning 4×4 factory for another.

A Breath of Fresh Air: New Yachting Design House Kunsen Drops Its K37 Cabrio and Tender Concepts
17 photos
Photo: Kunsen Yachts
Sometimes, it takes years to get a project going, especially if you want it to actually break the limits of design. This is particularly true for the boating industry, one that has centuries of R&D already behind it. However, some teams manage to bring something fresh to the game.
That team is none other than Kunsen, a young boat design house that’s been around since 2022 but who have just begun to show their teeth. That’s four years of racking their brains to come up with two tenders that go well beyond what the average millionaire toy can achieve, and if I may, we’re in for a real treat.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts After diving into the project before us, I realized that the Kunsen K37 lineup really does have a solid chance of making it into the real world, with the project even going as far as seeing real scale models. Buckle up, because this one is going places.
Now, when creating the Kunsen K37, the very first project for Kunsen, the brand chose to use it to establish a “design language” for themselves. As we can see, the Kunsen defines itself with clean lines, clearly defined spaces, and a slightly purist Scandinavian look.
But, once we peek beyond the design, we realize what Kunsen has achieved here. One of the initial tricks of the first K37 designs included the ability to hide the rear-facing lounge in the belly of the tender through a network of hydraulics that lowered or raised this feature into place.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts If it’s visible, we unlock the sun beds we see. If it’s hidden under the floor however, the K37 created a ground-level lounge while leaving the rear free of any obstructions, perfect for when you’re in some bay and decide to go for a swim.
A neat trick, to say the least and one that was ultimately ditched, and it’s easy to understand why; to make it work, entire new systems would need to be integrated into the tenders, not to mention pushing the boat to the brink of its weight limits or the production nightmares that may arise.
As the model progressed, Kunsen ultimately decided to craft two versions: the Cabrio and the Tender. The Cabrio is the one with the exposed rear sun bed, while the Tender places the lounge into the floor of the main deck.
Kunsen didn’t stop there, accompanying each of the designs with two bulwark terraces or balconies slash diving platforms. These not only expand the deck space, but also extend lounging options over open waters. Imagine hanging your feet off this ledge, taking a sip of champagne, and just taking it all in; there are no sharks in this daydream.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts Yet, we’re still not done with lounging options, with another sun bed visible at the bow of the boats and accessible by a walkway that runs along both sides of the wheelhouses. A teak deck balances the dark tones of the design but also stays as cool as possible while baking under constant exposure to the sun.
Be it the Tender or the Cabrio, both offer overnight and enclosed accommodations to their owners. The head, located in the lower level and at the front of the ship, places quite the amount of features at our disposal.
At the very tip of a 37, a large triangular bed is in place, and judging by the pads that make it up, it may be modular, capable of transforming into a U-shaped lounge when desired. Considering there’s a little wine bar and galley nearby, it would make a whole lot of sense.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts This kitchen is located on the starboard side of the ship, and port, the entrance to the head is occupied by a bathroom with toilet, shower, sink, and storage for essentials. This is the sort of bathroom you don’t often find in tenders such as these.
Since this team has plans to make these tenders a real product, they have also thought of the propulsion of the K37 class and worked out the placement of batteries, wiring, thrusters, engines, and inverters. It’s a hybrid setup that calls upon a mix of electric and combustion power to get moving. Dimensions are also complete; obviously, since there a scale model in the real world.
Photo: Kunsen Yachts That said, does the boating industry have a place for the K37 Tender and Cabrio? Personally, I’d say yes, but with a bit of a reservation based on the fact that these babies are pretty big, rolling in with a total length of 39,86 ft (12.15 m), so there needs to be an equally grand garage and those are typically found in superyachts.
Maybe Kunsen chooses to market these babies to coastline and island-hopping millionaires around the world as boats to be used as day boats, one with the ability to keep us under the stars too once we find some hidden cove somewhere.
Currently, Kunsen does have an “inquire” tab available on their website, so plans to make these babies a real deal is clearly much closer than we think.

2027 ROG 14RKB Continues To Have One of the Weirdest Bathrooms – Built for Tough Glamping Scenarios
26 photos
Photo: Encore RV
“ It’s not stupid if it works ” seems to be one of the phrases that comes to mind upon exploring the 2027 ROG 14RKB from Encore RV. It’s possible you have an idea of what this camper has in store based on previous model years, but if you’re not aware of what the 14RKB class brings to the table, prepare to be surprised, to say the least.
Ladies and gents, most campers on the market these days follow some very similar guidelines and styling, so when something that breaks the mold hits the scene , you can bet that the world is all eyes and ears. That’s precisely what happened when the ROG 14RKB was first introduced as a 2024 model.
Since then, outdoor lover after outdoor lover has had something to say about this one, sometimes, positive, sometimes, negative, and it all really makes sense.
Photo: Encore RV The 14RKB has always stood apart from other campers in its class with a rather unique interior for a square drop, with the highlight being the enclosed and complete wet bath inside, accessible via the rear. This means that you can shower and “meditate” in the morning without having to worry about prying eyes or creepy crawlers riding up your legs.
However, there is one massive catch here, and it’s the fact that showers are to be carried out sitting down. Simply put, there isn’t enough space to stand inside one of these bathrooms, making for some questionable acrobatics in order to clean your nooks and crannies.
It’s an odd position, to say the least, but does have one particular benefit that some people overlook: showering with a view. Since the bathroom is located at the rear of the unit, all you have to do is back this thing up to a mountain ledge looking east, and once the sun starts to rise over the horizon, wake up and take a shower while leaving the rear door open and enjoy . The same is true for other bathroom-oriented activities.
Photo: Encore RV One thing that I can say about the 14RKB is that is does truly invite its owners to take in the outside world, and aside from doing your thing with the bathroom door wide open, the kitchen also invites us to spend time in nature.
It does so by being mounted into the shell of the 14RKB. The main block is located on a slide-out that tucks into the rear right hand corner of the camper. This slide-out allows us to access a sink with faucet, cooktop, and ample storage for gas, water, and utensils, while a side-mounted griddle can also be called upon, located on the camping side of the unit.
The fridge, or should I say, fridges, are hidden behind a hatch over the griddle. Two are in place and completed the galley features. All this sits underneath a batwing awning, so we don’t sizzle away in the sun like our burger patties.
Photo: Encore RV While some reviews for the 14RKB mention that space is limited, I found the interior to be quite roomy, capable of handling a queen-sized modular mattress that can double as a seating arrangement for at least three people. I’m thinking folks were most likely referring to the size of the bathroom.
The interior is also equipped with ample storage, some of the largest bays I’ve seen in a camper of this style, and the possibility to add a TV. A sound system is in place, along with control panel too, window blinds, and even heating or AC, depending on what seasons of the year you want to tackle.
The 14RKB is also decently strong in the off-grid features department, with the manufacturer’s spec sheet showcasing battery arrays with as much as 400 Ah, solar panels of up to 400 W, and 3,000 W inverter, DC-DC charger, and a couple others. Two trim levels are available to choose from and more options do exist , including beefing up the suspension to an axle-less one and adding an articulating hitch.
To sum it all up, this one can take us off the beaten path, but does have some limits, one of which is a GVWR of 4,400 lbs (1,996 kg), with a dry weight, in its lightest configuration, of 2,283 lbs (1,035 kg).
Photo: Encore RV This leaves us with around 2,100 lbs of cargo-carrying capacity and the roof rack is the perfect place to add heavier items that can be exposed to the elements. I’s also a great place to add an RTT (roof-top tent), expanding this campers accommodation to an entire family of at least four guests, depending on the size of your tent.
I’m curious to hear your thoughts on what this RV brings to the table and how. Be sure to check out the little clip below for a better POV on things.
Last but not least, we have the price for one of these babies, which, according to Encore RV , is set with an MSRP of $36,321 (€33,120) for a baseline 2027 ROG 14RKB. Depending on trim levels and extras, a 2027 version can run close to $50K, with most dealers hovering around $45K.

The 2027 Hyundai Ioniq 6 N Costs Nearly BMW M2 Coupe Money in Canada
7 photos
Photo: Hyundai
The Ioniq 6 N electric performance sedan is a rather expensive car, as expected from the outset. Destination and delivery pushes the newcomer into BMW M2 Coupe territory, and worse still for the South Korean automaker, the quicker and faster Tesla Model 3 Performance will set you back CAD 74,990 as of this writing.
Whichever way you look at it, that's considerable money for an electric performance model with an undesirable badge. On the other hand, the South Korean colossus has designed something considerably more ambitious than an Ioniq 6 with nicer wheels and a sporty-looking steering wheel.
The first N-badged Ioniq 6 uses two electric drive units and an 84- kWh battery pack, with Hyundai Canada promising 601 horsepower by default or 641 when N Grin Boost kicks in. Peak torque is estimated at 568 pound-feet (770 Newton-meters), and N Launch Control helps the zero-emission model reach 100 kilometers per hour (62 miles per hour) in a claimed 3.2 clicks.
Pretty impressive on paper, but N Grin Boost only enables maximum output for up to 10 seconds at a time. Beyond the powertrain side of the deal, Hyundai made some interesting chassis updates to cope with the additional oomph, starting with electronically controlled suspension that uses stroke sensors to adjust damping according to the selected drive mode and road conditions.
An electronic limited-slip diff is on the menu as well. What Hyundai calls N Torque Distribution allows the driver to adjust the front-rear torque bias, and the company has further revised the suspension geometry for this application. From a structural standpoint, more structural adhesives and additional weld points help the N stand out from lesser versions of the Ioniq 6.
Photo: Hyundai Almost 20 percent better in terms of torsional stiffness compared to standard 6s, the N rolls on Pirelli P Zero rubber that comes with 20-inch forged aluminum wheels. The 275/35 tires and lightweight wheels frame performance brakes, with Hyundai listing four-piston calipers up front.
A rear wing also differentiates it from lesser 6s. All in all, Hyundai has clearly spent a lot of time and money addressing on-road and on-track capability. Its high-voltage battery features dedicated temperature management functions, with N Battery Preconditioning offering different settings for three driving scenarios: Drag, Sprint, and Endurance. As implied, Drag is tailored for short bursts of maximum launch and acceleration performance.
With the Ioniq 6 N, the South Korean manufacturer is also selling an experience. N e-Shift is a system that simulates the behavior of a transmission, manipulating torque in the process. N Active Sound+, meanwhile, is the function that generates driving sounds to bring the Ioniq 6 N closer to internal combustion models like Hyundai's very own Elantra N performance sedan.
While certain enthusiasts will enjoy this tech-heavy theater, others might question the need to imitate a gas-powered performance car in the first place. I certainly understand what Hyundai is trying to achieve here, but fake shifts and powertrain sounds will get old rather quickly from the driver's perspective.
On a different note, Hyundai Canada confirmed a NACS port for a direct connection between it and Tesla Superchargers. No need for adapters here! Unfortunately, the Canadian-market announcement does not provide specific driving range and energy consumption figures. In any case, the first units will hit dealer lots in early 2027, and Hyundai Canada underlines that limited quantities are expected.

Hyundai’s new IONIQ 3 checks all the boxes as an affordable EV: it offers over 300 miles of range, a practical interior, and Hyundai’s new Pleos infotainment system. So, will Hyundai bring it to the US?
Is Hyundai launching the IONIQ 3 in the US?
The Hyundai IONIQ 3 is now on sale across Europe and the UK as a smaller sibling to the IONIQ 5, positioned between the Inster EV and Hyundai Kona Electric.
Although it’s part of the IONIQ sub-brand, the IONIQ 3 features a new “Aero Hatch” design. The new look “reimagines the compact EV silhouette,” Hyundai said, designed to optimize efficiency and interior space.
The response so far has been “extraordinary,” Ashley Andrew, president of Hyundai Motor UK, said after launching the IONIQ 3 last month.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
According to Andrew, the compact EV received “more customers registering their interest before launch than any new Hyundai we’ve introduced in the UK,” and that’s including gas-powered and electric vehicles.
The first reviews of the IONIQ 3 have been overwhelmingly positive, highlighting its efficiency, practical interior, and affordable price tag.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by KindelAuto (@kindelauto)
So why doesn’t Hyundai sell it in the US? The IONIQ 3 was recently captured driving in public in the US, raising speculation, or perhaps hope, that it will come to the States after all.
The model spotted in the images from KindelAuto is the IONIQ 3 N Line, a sportier, higher-priced trim.
While it’s among the first sightings in the US, we have seen several Hyundai Motor Group electric vehicles testing in the US that are still not available and likely won’t ever be, such as Kia’s EV5 SUV and PV5 van.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 N-Line (Source: Hyundai UK)
The IONIQ 3 is built at Hyundai Motor’s Izmit, Turkey, plant and is specifically designed for European drivers.
We’ve reached out to Hyundai to see if anything has changed, but we haven’t heard back yet. We’ll update you when we hear more.
In Europe and the UK, Hyundai offers the IONIQ 3 with two battery packs: 42 kWh and 61 kWh. The base IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the 42 kWh battery starts at £18,495 ($25,000) OTR and offers up to 213 miles of WLTP range. That’s including the UK’s £3,750 Electric Car Grant.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior (Source: Hyundai)
The IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery starts at £21,995 ($29,000) and offers a “class-leading” WLTP range of up to 308 miles. That also includes the UK government ECG grant.
Measuring 4,155 mm (163.5″) long, 1,800 mm (70.9″) wide, and 1,505 mm (59.3″) high, with a wheelbase of 2,680 mm (105.5″), Hyundai’s electric hatch is even smaller than the Kia EV3 and Volkswagen ID.3.
The IONIQ 3 is also Hyundai’s first vehicle in Europe equipped with its new Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior with Pleos Connect infotainment system (Source: Hyundai)
Hyundai’s new system is more like using a smartphone. It’s based on the Android Automotive OS with apps and customizable screens, similar to Tesla models. It’s available in the IONIQ 3 with a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.
Unlike the larger IONIQ 5, the IONIQ 3 uses a 400V architecture. However, the 42 kWh battery can still recharge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes. The 61 kWh battery takes around 30 minutes.
In Germany and other European markets, Hyundai’s compact IONIQ 3 starts at about €28,950 ($33,000).
Hyundai IONIQ 3 (Source: Hyundai UK)
While Hyundai currently has no plans to bring the IONIQ 3 to the US, it does sell the IONIQ 5, built at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside Savannah, GA, alongside the three-row IONIQ 9.
Starting at about $35,000, Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 has remained among the top-selling electric vehicles in the US outside of the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.
In fact, Hyundai was just named the “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” by US News & World Report for the first time for 2027.
Hyundai’s sister company, Kia, also launched the 2027 EV3, which is now on sale starting at just $29,890 in the US.

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
Hot Wheels Unboxing: 10 Special Ferraris I Bought for November of 2026
142 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I wish every one of my diecast unboxing stories had a special topic. It’s easier said than done, even though I’m currently doing three of them each month. It’s particularly complicated when I decide to go for a special group of vehicles, like I have today.
There’s this one story I’ve been putting off for months now. As I know how complicated things can feel like in the hobby in 2026, I figured I’d do a comparison between Hot Wheels collectibles and cars from other brands.
I’ve got Matchbox, Maisto, Mini GT and IXO on my list. And I just wasn’t happy with the Car Culture 2-Pack I had bought for the story, so I upgraded to two Elite 64 models.
These should theoretically be on the same price level as Mini GT and IXO, but they’re more expensive than the Matchbox and Maisto models.
Oh well, it’s not like I could come with a definitive verdict on which brands you should focus on next in just one unboxing story. And anyway, you’re all free to choose the tiny cars that you genuinely love, regardless of my take on the topic.
Photo: autoevolution I’m just here to shine some light on the topic, hoping it will help you avoid spending too much in the wrong direction. I’ve been thinking about a Ferrari -only unboxing ever since Mattel announced the license renewal.
I’ve included some of the modern era castings in my stories since, but deep down I knew I wanted a closer look at what happened before 2015.
And I seized the opportunity the moment I spotted it, even though I paid circa $150 for just 10 Hot Wheels to get here. It might not seem like a lot if you’re an avid RLC collector.
However, from my perspective, it’s the same budget I’d spend on a complete Mainline case, or a Premium set of 10 cars plus something extra. And there’s only one vehicle on today’s list that has Real Riders wheels.
Ferrari F40 Photo: autoevolution I can tell you that this was easily the most expensive item here, but I knew I couldn’t let it go. After all, it’s also the only car here to feature an opening part.
It’s the kind of feature only a few Hot Wheels Ferraris have ever had. In the modern era, it only happened for the 1969 Ferrari 312 P and the F40, both of which were only available as Red Line Club models.
I’ve seen some people listing the latter for as much as $600 on eBay, which is absolutely ridiculous considering my dealer is selling a KKK 1:12th-scale F40 for less than $200.
To each their own I guess. The reason this F40 is so special is that it’s Larry Wood’s creation from the late ‘80s.
Photo: autoevolution It debuted in the 1989 Speed Fleet series and it was available all the way until its 2014 5-Pack release. I believe that was the only iteration that did not have a ZAMAC base, or an opening hood.
The one I have here was part of the Mainline series in the year 2000, and I absolutely love the card art from that period.
As for the car itself, it doesn’t look nearly as accurate as Shawn Moghadam modern Competizione casting. There’s no mechanism to keep the hood open, and it’s seriously loose and not a perfect fit like you’d get with Pop Race items these days.
I realize we’re into a different price league already, but that’s just how far the hobby has gone. Still, the nostalgia element balances things off, and this is certainly one of my collection’s highlights right now.
Ferrari 250 Photo: autoevolution The Ferrari 250 is the second of three Larry Wood -designed castings on today’s list, and it’s also the car with the second longest “career” here.
It was on the market for 18 years, starting with the 1991 Mainline series. Mattel was still using Black Wall wheels at the time, something that just wouldn’t work today.
Fast forward to 1995, its 5-pack iteration showed up with 7-Spoke wheels and a green paint job: I’d almost say it was identical to the car I have here.
It 1996 it showed up as a Treasure Hunt release, complete with Deep Dish Real Riders: I spotted one listed for $29 on eBay but it could be too good to be true.
Photo: autoevolution The one I found is #452 dating back to the 1996 Mainline series. You’ll notice the card art is a bit older by comparison and I enjoy seeing the back too: it’s a real time machine!
I don’t own any of the Speed Fleet, Speed Demons or Action Command collectibles there, but I’m certainly familiar with the Sharkcruiser as I have discussed it before.
This Metalflake Dark Green finish reminds me of Dave Weise’s ‘97 Corvette , but I couldn’t find it for a head-to-head comparison. In 1996, Mattel used three wheel variations on this car.
While I don’t think these 7-spokes are the best choice available, they’re still a clear sign that we’re dealing with an old collectible. You’ll find several iterations of the 250 with either Real Riders or Co-Molded wheels on the market, and it all came to an end in 2009 when it was reduced to a simple Mystery Car.
Ferrari F355 Photo: autoevolution The team in El Segundo has already “revived” the F40 for the modern era of Hot Wheels Ferraris, and you can already hunt for the 250 GTO if that’s what you like.
So, how about the F355? Ronald Wong designed the new one for next year’s Ferrari 80th Anniversary 5-Pack , and it’s quite stunning with that Nero Daytona (black) finish and those Star 5-Spoke wheels.
It will take a while before I can park it next to Larry Wood’s old design, though. This model debuted in the 1995 Model Series.
Coolio’s Gangsta's Paradise was the top hit on Billboard’s list that year, Bill Clinton was serving his first term as the President of the United States of America and Blizzard Entertainment had released Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness (one of my all-time favorite video games!).
Photo: autoevolution Now that I’ve hopefully transported you back to the mid ‘90s, imagine what owning a Ferrari F355 must have been like. My uncle had a Kadett at the time, and it felt like a rocket ship with 81 horsepower on tap, while the F355 was packing 375 hp from its 3.5 liter V8.
I just had a quick look at BaT’s auction results, and prices seem to vary between $90,000 to $355,355 for one of these cars. That means I’ll have to settle for the 1/64th-scale version for now. At least I’m the happy owner of one of the first iterations to ever come out of the factory.
I’d give up the 5-Dot wheels for a set of Saw-blade rims any day of the week. You can also opt for three other designs in that department, as they were all available that same year.
While the 355 got a Treasure Hunt release in 1996, its final version is likely still the most desired one as it was part of the Ferrari Racer series and had CM6 rims to show off. It could cost around $100 if you’re willing to go that far.
Ferrari F50 Spider Photo: autoevolution That was the last of the yellow Ferraris for today’s story. There’s no Nero Daytona in here today, so you’ll have to settle for two more grey ones and five cars in the iconic red finish.
At least the 250 was special in green, right? I know asking 100 people what their ultimate dream car is could render 100 different answers.
I’m sure some of them will include the McLaren F1, the Lamborghini Diablo and the Ferrari F40. But I’ve been stuck thinking about the F50 ever since I was six or seven years old and my mom bought me a Bburago version of the car.
Being able to race it in Need for Speed II around the same period further fueled that fire, and I almost fainted when I saw one in the real world back in 2015. If I could only ever drive one Ferrari in my life, this would be the one.
Photo: autoevolution And there’s no better way to enjoy that F1-derived V12 in the back than by having the top down. Michael Kollins designed both this Spider version and the Challenge model, and you could say the latter was a bit more successful having been available between 1999 and 2013.
The Spider debuted in the 1996 First Editions series alongside the 1996 Mustang GT which I just recently unboxed. It’s always exciting to have the first version of a certain Hot Wheels item in your collection, and I don’t think I can ever let it go.
My dealer also had the Metalflake Purple version of the car (last one to ever come out of the factory), but I just had to choose this red car even though it cost twice as much.
You can find it in yellow too and I truly hope that’s what Mattel will use for Ronald Wong’s casting next. The old car definitely feels outdated when parked next to the modern era casting, which doesn’t make it any less exciting.
Ferrari Testarossa Photo: autoevolution The Ferrari F40 is the heaviest collectible on today’s list: at 56 grams it’s in the Top100 out of a total of almost 400 Hot Wheels I’ve unboxed since last year.
The Ferrari Testarossa isn’t that far behind, as it proves Mattel’s products in the ‘90s had more metal in them than they do today (even when comparing old Mainline to new Premium cars).
Of course this isn’t a definitive verdict, and I guess some people might not even care about the way these items “perform” on the scales.
I enjoying documenting the observation, though. At first, I thought the Testarossa I had just bought was Larry Wood’s design from the late ‘80s. I realized something was off after not being able to identify any variation of it with the 5-Dot wheels.
Photo: autoevolution Mattel retired the design in 1998, making way for the F512M/Testarossa that Michael Kollins worked on (he designed nine Ferraris during his tenure, and we’ve got five of them here today). The Metalflake Silver version was the First Edition release in 1998, rolling on either 5DOT or 5-Spoke rims.
They both had a metal base though, and I wish I could get a closer look at the 1999 Treasure Hunt iteration with the PC5 wheels.
Given how window shopping is completely free, I’d also probably skip the Ferrari Racer Testarossa and go straight for the 2013 Retro Entertainment: Miami Vice that also closed the chapter for the design.
I used a small flashlight when taking a photo of the rear section of the new and old cars so you can see the difference 30+ years have made. I’m almost certain collectors would keep buying modern variations of the ‘90s casting as it’s still fairly impressive today.
Ferrari 360 Modena Photo: autoevolution Nissan reportedly built just under 12,000 units of the Skyline GT-R (R34), while most people will tell you Ferrari probably only made less than 9,000 360 Modenas.
So, if you ignore the Spider version of the Italian sports car, it’s quite a bit rarer than “Godzilla”. Now, a quick look at the used market: The cheapest GT-R on BaT traded hands for $105,000 this year, while the most expensive one went for $444,444.
Meanwhile, someone was lucky enough to get a Modena for $70,666, while the coolest one sold for $325,000. Let’s not talk about Challenge Stradale options though. What I’m trying to say here is this.
If you could only afford one car, you’d have to be out of your damn mind to pick the GT-R instead of the 360 Modena. I don’t even care about lap times, running costs, or tuning possibilities, these machines are in different leagues.
Photo: autoevolution And the fun part is that you can still find a way to buy the Ferrari, even if you’re not a millionaire. Yes, I am worried about the maintenance at this point, but it’s not something you have to deal with in the 1/64th-scale Universe.
Also, can you believe this casting is almost 30 years old at this point? I’d be shocked if Mattel doesn’t come up with a modern era version of it in 2027 or 2028 the latest.
But I can also survive on collecting more variations of the design Michael Kollins worked on. Mine is another First Editions release, and I’m happy to report that it has a metal base. In 2001 it showed up in black with PR5 wheels, and you’ll find the same design on a few more iterations.
I know some collectors will be eager to look for the four Ferrari Racer models, but those can easily cost over $50 a pop. The Auto Affinity: Got Speed version will only be half as expensive and it’s running on genuine Real Riders rims!
Ferrari F355 Challenge Photo: autoevolution You could say 1999 was a good year for Hot Wheels Ferrari enthusiasts. Not only did we get the 360 Modena, but also the F355 Challenge back then.
I’m unsure why the latter isn’t a “First Editions” release though. This thing had a metal base, which is why it weighs 47 grams, on par with the newer basic GMC Motorhome and the premium McLaren Speedtail I unboxed recently.
Buying a real world F355 Challenge might be complicated, considering only 108 were reportedly built. What Michael Kollins achieved here is seriously impressive, and it makes Larry Wood’s old F355 look seriously outdated by comparison.
While I’d normally be annoyed by the gray finish, the stripes running down the middle and the racing decals are a big plus.
Photo: autoevolution We’ve got Beta Tools, Magneti Marelli and Pirelli to name a few, and then there’s the spoiler. It just needs detailed tail lights and Real Riders wheels at this point.
Mattel switched to yellow for the next two years and four variations, and a red F355 Challenge didn’t show up until 2003.
For 2007, 2008 and 2009 it advanced to the Ferrari Racer series and even I have to admit that the black one was amazing with orange wheels on.
This casting has just as long of a lifespan as the 360 Modena and the 333 SP I’m about to dive into next.
Ferrari 333 SP Photo: autoevolution If you were looking for the fastest car on today’s list, you’ve just found it. It’s obviously not the only one here with a V12 engine inside but it’s a racing machine first and foremost and it weighs less than a first-generation Mazda MX-5 (under 2,000 lbs/907 kg!).
Ferrari only made 40 of them (with Dallara and Michelotto onboard the project as well). I think you could have bought one for less than $1 million back in 2011, and it won’t be remotely as easy to do so today.
I’ve seen one racing down the main straight at Mugello about a decade ago, and it’s probably the closest I’ve gotten to a ‘90s F1 machine engaged in WOT mode.
You have to hear it to believe it! The 333 SP was the first Hot Wheels Ferrari Mark Jones worked on, and it wouldn’t be his last. His 156 is on my Must Have list for the near future, and the same goes for his Enzo and 250 LM.
Photo: autoevolution Honestly, it’s almost surreal for me to have the first-ever release of the 333 SP in my collection, even though I’m not completely happy with the Wire Spoke wheels.
The PR5s are slightly better, and I wish the team would have used something similar on the Hall of Fame: Milestone Moments too.
The blue livery on the 2002 Ferrari 5-Pack variation is just as enticing, and I’m not even upset this is one of the lightest items on my list for today. I just wish I still had some of the other ‘90s IMSA Racers at home for the photo shoot: both the Cadillac LMP and Riley & Scott MK III are long gone.
Now I suddenly have the urge to go back to the original Assetto Corsa for a lap in the Porsche 917/30.
Ferrari 550 Maranello Photo: autoevolution I don’t know about you, but I’m not a fan of Porsches or Ferraris that have a front-mounted engine. Some of them can still be incredibly fast, but I feel a big part of the supercar experience is gone once you choose that layout.
You’ll notice that the 550 Maranello is only one of two such machines on this list, and we could give the 250 a pass considering how old and rare it is.
The 550 debuted back in 1996, and my first contact with it happened in circa 2002 with Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2.
That game featured the rarer, Barchetta Pininfarina version, though, and I can’t say it had any effect on me as I was happier in either the 360 Spider or the F50.
Photo: autoevolution I might just start a special “First Editions” display at home when I’ll have enough space to do so, as this 550 Maranello was part of that series in the year 2000.
I’ve see photos of an alternate release for this debut iteration which had silver headlights and I’m glad to have the regular version instead.
Production ended in 2013 with a Speed Machines variation that didn’t even have the Co-Molded wheels on anymore.
You’ll have to search for the 2011 550 Maranello to enjoy those, or the 2009 Ferrari Racer if you don’t mind paying $40 to $100 for one. You won’t find any Real Riders rims here, and the 575 GTC didn’t get them either.
Ferrari Enzo Photo: autoevolution I missed the pre-order window on this year’s Boulevard Mix 4, and I knew that meant I would never be able to find the Ferrari Enzo for its regular retail price.
When someone in our local collector’s group listed it for $16, I immediately ordered two as I was sure my buddy Omar would want it as well.
It was ultimately a bit cheaper than the F50, which I paid about $19 for. At least I secured a pre-order for the F40, which means chasing after the 288 GTO is the next logical step to get all the Big 5s under the same roof.
The LaFerrari is the one I’m least excited about. There’s even less nostalgia involved with the F80, which is bound to show up within the next two to three years.
Photo: autoevolution Anyway, Ronald Wong did an amazing job with the Enzo, and this thing definitely sets a new standard for future Boulevard/Car Culture collectibles.
A comparison with Tomica’s take on the car might have been interesting if it didn’t have those hideous wheels on.
I haven’t heard any news about a new variation for 2027, but I’m keeping my fingers crossed for a Giallo Modena finish. How long before we get a Ferrari-exclusive set?
The Big 5 makes the most sense, and it could easily become one the most hyped mixes in Hot Wheels history when it happens. I say “when” because I’m certain there’s no need to use “if” here. I’ll be back with my next unboxing story soon!

Peñasquito mine is the largest individual silver-producing mine, by output. ( Image courtesy of Newmont via Flickr. )
By: Staff Writer November 24, 2026
Global silver mine production is expected to remain virtually unchanged this year despite a sixth consecutive annual market deficit.
Demand is forecast to exceed supply by 35 million oz. in 2026, bringing the cumulative shortfall since 2021 to a projected 746 million oz., according to figures prepared by research firm Metals Focus for the Silver Institute. That represents nearly 90% of annual global mine output, projected at 834 million oz. this year.
“Peak silver scarcity is clearly in the rear-view mirror,” Deutsche Bank head of metals research Daniel Ghali wrote in an Oct. 2 report. He forecast that weakening industrial demand could tip the market into surplus as early as 2027.
The prospect of a surplus despite stagnant mine production highlights the limited response of silver supply to higher prices. New research by GEM Mining Consulting suggests the market’s ability to rebalance hinges more on changes in consumption, recycling and inventories than on miners expanding operations.
Between 2021 and 2025, annual silver demand averaged 1.17 billion oz., up 20% from the preceding four-year period, when the market recorded surpluses. Average annual mine output declined by 0.9%, while recycling increased by 15% between those periods.
The consultancy’s statistical analysis suggests production has a stronger relationship with prices from two or three years earlier than with current market conditions, although the limited number of observations warrants caution.
Byproduct dependence
Primary silver mines accounted for just 26.1% of global mine supply in 2025, down from 28.7% in 2019 and the lowest proportion in Metals Focus’ data series, according to GEM’s comparison of annual surveys.
Lead and zinc operations contributed 29.4%, followed by copper mines at 28% and gold operations at 15.9%. Other sources account for the remainder.
“For them, a higher silver price improves revenues, but hardly justifies, on its own, extracting more ore,” Patricio Faúndez of GEM Mining Consulting wrote of operations that produce silver as a byproduct.
GEM calculates that silver output from copper mines increased by 24.5% between 2019 and 2025, supported by expanding global copper production, project ramp-ups in Chile and higher grades in Peru. Production from lead and zinc operations declined by 7.3%, while gold-related output edged 2% higher.
Chile illustrates the disconnect. Silver production from the country’s copper mines fell by 10% over the same period despite a 95% increase in inflation-adjusted silver prices, according to GEM’s analysis of Chilean Copper Commission data.
Dedicated silver operations have also struggled, with output falling by 7.9% between 2019 and 2025 amid declining grades and operational challenges, according to GEM.
Metals Focus expects primary mines to add 6.5 million oz. this year, largely through operational improvements in Mexico. Higher prices lifted their margins by 187% in the first half of 2026 despite a 47% increase in all-in sustaining costs.
The increase represents less than one-fifth of this year’s projected market shortfall.
Demand destruction
Silver briefly surpassed $120 (C$172) per oz. in January before retreating to $52 by Nov. 4, according to the Silver Institute. The earlier rally accelerated efforts among industrial consumers to reduce their reliance on the metal.
Deutsche’s October report estimated that global silver consumption in solar applications would decline by more than 20% this year, with Chinese demand falling 33%. Manufacturers are adopting thinner electrical contacts, silver-coated copper pastes and alternative cell designs to reduce costs.
Silver consumption per solar cell was forecast to fall 17% this year in the bank’s report.
Metals Focus, meanwhile, expects overall demand to decline by 5% in 2026 as jewellery and silverware purchases weaken. Recycling is projected to increase by 6%, reaching its highest level since 2012.
London’s commercial vaults held about 929 million oz. at the end of October, down 0.3% from September, according to the London Bullion Market Association. Deutsche’s October report estimated more than 300 million oz. were freely available for purchase at the end of August, up 70% since October 2025.
“Ultimately, this ties into the significant deterioration in silver’s demand profile, primarily relating to thrifting trends, which now threaten to create a glut,” Ghali wrote.
Deutsche’s October report forecast that spot silver prices would average $70 per oz. in the second quarter of 2027, with investment flows becoming increasingly important to the metal’s performance as industrial demand weakens.
For primary silver producers, the prospect of a surplus emerging before meaningful new mine capacity comes online could complicate expansion decisions, even as elevated prices support profitability.

Image: Volkswagen Group
Volkswagen is giving EV drivers in Germany a reason to plug in at home, even if they don’t need a charge. VW’s charging subsidiary, Elli, is launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) program in December that pays drivers up to €720 in the first year for keeping a compatible EV plugged in.
What drivers get paid for
The bidirectional home charger costs €1,995, including tax and shipping. Installation is extra.
Elli pays a plug-in bonus of €0.24 for each eligible hour the EV is plugged into the Elli BiDi DC charger. Sessions have to last at least three hours, and drivers need 250 plugged-in hours a month – a little over eight hours a day on average – to earn the full €60 monthly bonus. VW estimates the full first-year bonus could cover the electricity for around 15,500 km (9,600 miles) in an ID.3 Neo Trend, assuming electricity costs €0.33 per kWh.
Elli’s “V2G Flow” electricity plan covers the home and the car. Elli expects to offer a separate payment later under its “V2G Return” plan, at €0.40 for each kWh the car sends back to the grid. Drivers use Elli’s app to set when they need the car and how much charge they want by then. The system handles charging and, when available, sends power back to the grid according to that schedule.

What’s needed to sign up
The 11 kW DC charger supports 400- and 800-volt EVs, but eligibility depends on the model and which functions VW has enabled. The offer spans Volkswagen, Cupra, Škoda, and Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles; the latter has its own ordering process. Drivers also need a compatible smart meter and must complete Elli’s online site check and obtain an installation quote before they can order the charger.
BMW and E.ON opened orders in Germany for their home V2G package for the iX3 in February. VW is bringing its offer to four brands, and it says around 360,000 of its EVs built on VW Group’s shared electric platform in Germany have the technical groundwork for bidirectional charging. Drivers will still need to check whether their specific EV qualifies.
Elli is working with bidirectional charging company The Mobility House Energy to pool the available battery capacity of participating EVs. It plans to expand V2G to more European markets in 2027 and launch a separate vehicle-to-home (V2H) product that would let households use electricity stored in their EV, including surplus rooftop solar saved for later use.

New Vertical Powertrain Center for the Valo eVTOL Unveiled in Bristol
7 photos
Photo: Vertical Aerospace
Vertical Aerospace, one of the most important AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) companies in Europe right now, is celebrating another milestone, with construction completed on its brand-new Vertical Powertrain Center in Bristol. The facility isn’t operational yet, but it aims to boost battery production for electric aircraft considerably.
The eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) scene in Europe is looking pretty dim, sadly, with a lot fewer manufacturing still standing and going strong. The tragic fate of Germany’s Volocopter, one of the most highly-anticipated air taxis made in Europe, highlighted once more the financial fragility of AAM startups in an industry that is still in its early beginnings.
Vertical Aerospace has remained one of the very few European eVTOL makers with solid plans to actually produce their aircraft on the Old Continent. At the same time as developing and upgrading its flagship aircraft, named Valo, Vertical has also worked steadily on building a robust manufacturing infrastructure in support of future commercial operations.
The Vertical Energy Center (VEC) opened in 2023, covering 15,000 square feet. This is where the batteries that were used for Vertical’s piloted flights over the past three years have been designed, tested, and produced. This year, VEC reached a new level, by producing the first all-electric Valo battery on its upgraded assembly line.
There’s also the Aircraft Assembly Center, officially opened at Cotswold Airport in September. Now, Vertical has announced that a new center, the Vertical Powertrain Center, is finalized and ready for equipment installation.
This new center, scheduled to kick off operations by next year, is located next to VEC in Bristol, and as its name suggests, will be exclusively dedicated to electric and hybrid-electric powertrain engineering, system integration, and battery testing.
The Powertrain Center is twice as big as VEC, unfolding over 30,000 square feet, and Vertical expects it will triple battery-production capacity in the near future. With a Valo eVTOL expected to require approximately 20 battery packs throughout its life cycle, this new Center is also expected to generate income for the company beyond individual aircraft sales.
More than that, the Center’s production will expand beyond eVTOL operations, through battery recycling and other re-use applications that will support other sectors in aerospace and mobility.
Vertical’s plans sound promising, but he only question left is where will it manufacture its actual aircraft? The location of its first full-scale aircraft production site is yet to be unveiled, but Vertical confirmed plans to announce it before the end of this year, so stay tuned.
Vertical’s flagship aircraft, Valo, is a four-passenger eVTOL primarily aimed at air taxi operations. Commercially, the UK-based company has secured more than 1,500 pre-orders for Valo, but is also working on a hybrid-electric version with better range, that could expand to multiple applications beyond air taxi service.

Hot Wheels Goes After LEGO with Its Own Formula 1 Car Collections
31 photos
Photo: Hot Wheels
At the end of last week, Danish toymaker LEGO announced it is releasing minifigures of all this season's Formula 1 drivers, accompanied by all 11 cars that were on the grid of F1 races these past few months. It didn't take long for competitor Hot Wheels to reply.
The Mattel-owned brand already had such a collection of 1:64-scale cars in its portfolio, but it was, until now, incomplete. That changes from early next year, when the representations of newcomers Cadillac Formula 1 and Audi Revolut F1 will join the party for the first time.
Their arrival marks the completion of the collection, with all 11 teams now represented, each with two cars (unlike LEGO , which offers a single car per team). The refreshed range will become available at retailers in a gradual manner, starting early next year.
The first to land will be Sergio Perez’s No. 11 Cadillac and Gabriel Bortoleto’s No. 5 Audi Revolut, which will hit shelves in February 2027. Valtteri Bottas’ No. 77 and Nico Hulkenberg’s No. 27 will make their entrance later in the year.
Technically speaking, these new toys are nowhere near what LEGO has to offer, in terms of everything from complexity to size. These are small die-casts, unlike the DIY plastic cars the Danes throw on the market, and are priced as such: $9.99 each (LEGO's cost $29.99).
For that cash, collectors get access to replicas of the race cars wearing their updated liveries, but also the technical and visual modifications that were enforced this year: new front and rear wing geometry and updated overall proportions.
Each of the cars, sold as part of the Hot Wheels Premium Formula 1 collection, comes with a metal body and chassis, wheels shod in Real Riders tires, and a display plinth so that they can be properly shown off.
Those wishing to get their hands on the complete collection can opt for the Hot Wheels Formula 1 Season Display Set, which, at $220, throws in all 22 cars, but also a double-sided display mat so that they can be properly lined up. This collection becomes available next week, on December 4.
Aside from the cars mentioned above, there are a couple of side dishes related to F1 that can be had as well. Track sets selling from $28.99 to $149.99 allow people, among other things, to recreate races in either head-to-head or side-by-side modes, but only from the spring of 2027, when they arrive in stores.
Finally, a Silver Series Tooned Formula 1 set takes all the 11 cars from the 2026 season and morphs them into things with exaggerated proportions and unique styling. Each of them, also in 1:64 scale, sells for $3.99 and comes complete with authentic team logos and sponsorship details, front and rear wing decorations, and team-specific driver helmet colors.
There is no fixed release date for these things, as they'll become available throughout the year.

The 2027 NoBo 21.1 Is a Slide-Free Off-Grid Travel Trailer With a Stylish Look and Modern Comfort
19 photos
Photo: The RV Hunter/YouTube screenshot
A travel trailer for couples should have a few essential features to be considered comfortable and practical. It should have a usable kitchen, a proper bedroom with walk-around bed, comfortable seating, a functional bathroom, and enough storage to make longer trips enjoyable. An efficient layout that gives you enough room to move around, steady power, a reliable construction, and the ability to travel beyond campgrounds also matter.
The 2027 No Boundaries 21.1 travel trailer from Forest River checks most of these boxes, while also adding a few interesting touches of its own, resulting in an appealing home away from home.
Introduced as a new floorplan for the 2027 model year, this couples’ RV is designed to make the traveling experience better than ever with a rugged construction, a spacious interior, and all the amenities needed for comfortable, extended journeys. It is also equipped with off-grid equipment, and the interior offers a high level of style and refinement.
The No Boundaries 21.1 is dual-axle travel trailer with a floorplan that has two entries and no slide-outs. It measures 29.5 feet (8.9 meters) long and 96 inches (243 cm) wide, and even without relying on slide-outs, it manages to fit a front kitchen, comfortable theater seating, a separate dining area, a walk-through bathroom, and a private rear bedroom. That’s a lot of separate areas in a couples-oriented travel trailer, especially since it doesn’t make the distinct zones feel like they’re meant to do several jobs.
Photo: The RV Hunter/YouTube screenshot Like all the models in the NoBo lineup , it boasts a solid construction, with welded aluminum framing, superior Azdel composite panels, a fiberglass front cap, and an enclosed underbelly with forced heat. This is a construction meant to resist moisture and prevent problems like mold and delamination.
Campers who want to embark on more adventurous trips can equip the trailer with the Beast Mode Package, which adds an independent suspension system for handling rougher roads and off-road-style tires. The optional upgrade also includes 400 watts of solar and a 2,000W inverter with controller, making the RV better suited for camping in off-grid locations.
Finished in an eye-catching green-and-brown color scheme, the NoBo 21.1 comes with exterior equipment clearly intended to encourage outdoor living. There’s a large awning on the campsite, an exterior kitchen with a griddle underneath, an LP quick connect for hooking up additional propane appliances, marine speakers, and a hot-and-cold outdoor shower.
Photo: The RV Hunter/YouTube screenshot Other practical features include a rear pass-through storage compartment for tools and outdoor equipment, power tongue jack, space for two batteries, a bumper-mounted spare tire, and a 2-inch receiver. Preparation for a backup camera and Starlink connectivity is also available.
The interior floor plan is designed to keep the main living areas open and connected while providing a sense of separation for a private bedroom. With a front kitchen, central lounge and dining area, and a rear bedroom, there is an easy flow between areas.
One of the aspects that make the interior more distinctive and definitely different from other models on the market is the color scheme. Instead of the typical neutral palette, this travel trailer features green cabinetry, brown accents, and contrasting white surfaces that give the space more personality and warmth.
Photo: The RV Hunter/YouTube screenshot As mentioned, this floor plan has two entrances, and one of them opens into the front kitchen, which spans the entire width of the trailer and is decently equipped for cooking on the road. It features ample counter space that integrates not one but two power towers, an undermount stainless-steel sink with a two-sided faucet and cup rinser, a three-burner cooktop and a microwave/air-fryer combo. A large 10.7 cu.ft. refrigerator and a pantry for groceries are also included.
The central living area is compact but cleverly arranged to ensure comfort. There are two theater-style recliners accompanied by dinner trays and overhead storage on one side and a dining table for two, more storage under a long worktop, and a fireplace on the other.
From the lounge, a space-saving pocket door leads to the small walk-through bathroom, which feels very stylish with its longhorn wallpaper. It includes a shower with built-in shelves for toiletries, a rolling door, and a skylight overhead. The space is also fitted with a toilet, a vanity sink, and a floor-to-ceiling linen cabinet.
Photo: The RV Hunter/YouTube screenshot Another pocket door separates the bathroom from the rear bedroom. Designed as a private space for relaxation, this room features a walkaround queen-size bed with storage arranged around it, including tall wardrobes with hanging space and overhead cabinets. The bed also has built-in pull-out drawers for extra storage.

China will keep tighter rules on U.S.-bound shipments of gallium, germanium and antimony on hold for two more months, through Jan. 27, 2027, the Commerce Ministry said Tuesday.
The existing suspension was due to expire Nov. 27. The December 2024 rules generally bar export licences for U.S.-bound dual-use items involving the three metals or superhard materials. Dual-use items have both civilian and military applications.
The extension also covers stricter checks on buyers and uses of certain U.S.-bound graphite products. China still requires export licences for controlled products and bars exports of dual-use goods to U.S. military users or for U.S. military use.
China produced an estimated 99% of the world’s primary low-purity gallium in 2025. U.S. net import reliance for the metal was 100%, and integrated circuits accounted for 73% of U.S. gallium consumption, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.
Rio Tinto (LSE, ASX, NYSE: RIO) and Indium Corp. first recovered gallium at Indium’s research facility in Rome, N.Y., in May 2025, using material from Rio’s Vaudreuil alumina refinery in Quebec. Rio expects a pilot plant at its Saguenay complex to start operating in 2027. A planned demonstration plant at the same site could produce up to 4 tonnes a year.
Separately, Beijing has suspended its October 2025 controls on certain rare earths and related technology through Jan. 10, 2027. Licensing rules imposed in April 2025 on shipments of certain rare earths and magnets remain in force.
